value: integer cents
why: All money values (unit prices, line amounts, discounts, tax, totals) are integers in cents; no floats. invoice.py formats cents as dollars with 2 decimals.

value: decimal.Decimal, exact, e.g. Decimal("8.25"), Decimal("10"), Decimal("0")
why: Percentages are decimal.Decimal values, never floats. invoice.py formats them without trailing zeros.

value: pricing.get_unit_price_cents(sku) -> int or None (None = unknown SKU); pricing.get_customer_discount_percent(customer_id) -> Decimal or None (None = unknown customer)
why: invoice.py calls these two functions for every line and for the customer. Unknown returns None, not an exception.

value: tax.calculate_tax(customer_id, taxable_cents) -> (tax_cents: int, tax_percent: Decimal); unknown customer -> (0, Decimal("0")). tax_cents is already rounded half-up to the cent by tax.py.
why: invoice.py never computes tax rules; it passes the customer id and the taxable amount (subtotal minus discount, in cents) and displays the returned percent and amount.

value: discount_cents = (subtotal_cents * discount_percent / 100) rounded half-up to the cent, computed with Decimal; tax base = subtotal_cents - discount_cents
why: Defines the exact discount arithmetic so the pricing and invoice sides agree. Applies to invoice.py only; pricing.py only supplies the percent.

value: integer cents: every monetary amount in the system is an int number of cents (e.g. 1250 = 12.50). Never floats.
why: Avoids float rounding errors in tax and totals; pricing.py catalog already stores price_cents.

value: Region is a two-letter uppercase US state code string, e.g. TX, OR, NY. Tax keys its rules on this value. Unknown customer -> error, never a default region.
why: Tax rules (agent2) need the customer's region; pricing owns customer data.

value: pricing.get_item(sku: str) -> Item; pricing.get_customer(customer_id: str) -> Customer; Item is a frozen dataclass(sku, name, price_cents:int, category:str); Customer is a frozen dataclass(id, name, discount_pct:int 0..100, region:str). why: Single lookup surface for invoice.py; discount is customer data so pricing applies it; tax stays out of pricing.

Region as two-letter code is what tax needs. For tax.py: a region that is None or not in rates.csv gets 0% tax (RULES.md 'unknown customer pays 0%'). Whether an unknown customer id errors is pricing's decision.

discounted_unit_price_cents rounds per unit, but RULES.md defines tax base = (sum of undiscounted taxable line amounts) * (100 - discount_pct)/100 with one rounding of the tax at the end. tax.py needs undiscounted line amounts (price_cents * qty), item.category, and customer.discount_pct / customer.region. The discounted helper may stay for display but must not feed the tax path. Everything else in PRICING_API is acceptable to me.

Conflicts with PRICING_API (agent1). It lacks item category (needed for exemptions) and customer region (needed for tax). Please settle on one pricing API; I support PRICING_API with the change above.

Conflicts with RULES.md: the discount applies to the taxable (non-exempt) amount only, with no rounding before tax. This proposal discounts the full subtotal including exempt items and rounds the discount to the cent first, which can change tax by a cent. Discount arithmetic will live in tax.py (see tax_api v2).

tax has no customer data, so it cannot take customer_id; it needs the region. It also needs item categories for exemptions, so invoice cannot pre-filter taxable amounts without implementing tax rules. See tax_api v2.
Accept. tax.py receives the region from invoice.py; if the region is None or not in rates.csv, tax is 0%.

value: tax.calculate_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> (tax_cents: int, tax_percent: Decimal). Inputs supplied by invoice.py from pricing: region = pricing.get_customer_region(customer_id) (customer_region); discount_pct = pricing.get_customer_discount_percent(customer_id) (Decimal or None = 0); lines = list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) for every line item, amount_cents = unit price * qty, UNDISCOUNTED; category = pricing.get_item_category(sku) (NEW function, str, None = not exempt). tax.py: drops lines whose category is in exempt_categories.csv; taxable = sum of the rest; base = taxable * (100 - discount_pct) / 100; tax = base * tax_pct / 100 in exact Decimal, rounded once half-up to integer cents. region None or not in rates.csv -> (0, Decimal('0')). tax_percent = the rate from rates.csv as Decimal.
why: tax_api v1 forces invoice.py to apply exemptions and the discount, which RULES.md assigns to tax. The v1 topic is still open with my objection and the tool cannot revise an open version, so this new topic states the corrected interface.

why: Required by tax_interface (agent2) for exemption rules; pricing owns item data. pricing_api v1 is open and cannot be revised, so this is a separate topic.
